copy.en: Healthy mucus is usually clear or whitish, but it can change color once you get sick.
copy.tl: Karaniwang malinaw o maputi ang malusog na uhog, pero maaari itong magbago ng kulay kapag may sakit ka.
copy.bis: Kasagaran tin-aw o maputi ang himsog nga sip-on, apan mahimong mausab ang kolor kung magsakit ka.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a feeding behavior but does not observe or describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor identify their role in movement or food gathering.

copy.en: When it spots a moving insect, the mudskipper quickly lunges and snaps it up before it can escape.
copy.tl: Kapag may nakitang gumagalaw na insekto, mabilis na sumusugod at sumasakmal ang mudskipper bago ito makatakas.
copy.bis: Kon makakita og naglihok nga insekto, paspas nga mosulong ug motukob ang mudskipper sa dili pa kini makaikyas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the mudskipper also snacks on small worms and snails that live in the mud
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)

assignedReviews.reason: A mudskipper diet is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en: Besides insects, the mudskipper also snacks on small worms and snails that live in the mud!
copy.tl: Bukod sa insekto, kumakain din ang mudskipper ng maliliit na bulate at susô na nakatira sa putikan!
copy.bis: Gawas sa insekto, mokaon usab ang mudskipper og gagmay nga ulod ug susô nga nagpuyo sa lapok!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Smooth muscles inside your intestines gently squeeze and pull on their own to push food along
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions intestines and how food is pushed along, but does not identify the specific parts (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) from pictures or labeled diagrams, nor describe how those named parts work. It only touches on intestinal smooth muscle action, which is background to the digestive system but not the competency's identification/description task.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Smooth muscles inside your intestines gently squeeze and pull on their own to push food along
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using a labeled diagram, trace how food travels through the digestive tract and explain how different digestive processes work, including mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, and elimination
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires using a labeled diagram to trace food through the digestive tract and explain digestive processes (mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, elimination). The card has no labeled diagram, does not trace food through the tract, and only mentions peristalsis-like smooth muscle action in the intestines. This is a small related detail, not direct support for the required diagram-based tracing and process explanation.

copy.en:
How does your gut push food along on its own?

Smooth muscles inside your intestines gently squeeze and pull on their own to push food along as it's digested — and they keep working even while you sleep!
copy.tl:
Paano itinutulak ng bituka ang pagkain kahit hindi mo iniisip?

Ang mga smooth muscle sa loob ng iyong bituka ay marahang humihila at pumipiga nang kusa para itulak ang pagkain habang tinutunaw — gumagana pa ito kahit natutulog ka!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagtulod sa imong tinai sa pagkaon bisan wala nimo hunahunaa?

Ang mga smooth muscle sa sulod sa imong tinai hinay nga mobira ug mopiga sa iyang kaugalingon aron itulod ang pagkaon samtang gihilis kini — nagpadayon gihapon kini bisan natulog ka!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The muskmelon is a large, sweet fruit with juicy flesh and many seeds inside, growing on a trailing vine.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the fruit of a muskmelon, not the outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in water and nutrient uptake. It only shares the broad plant topic.

copy.en: The muskmelon is a large, sweet fruit with juicy flesh and many seeds inside, growing on a trailing vine.
copy.tl: Ang melon ay malaki at matamis na prutas na may makatas na laman at maraming buto sa loob, tumutubo sa gumagapang na halaman.
copy.bis: Ang melon dako ug tam-is nga prutas nga adunay tubigon nga unod ug daghang liso sa sulod, motubo sa nagakamang nga tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If a mutation happens in reproductive cells, it can be passed down to the offspring.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe mutations as changes in DNA or chromosomes and discuss some of the factors that cause mutations, such as infectious agents, radiation, and chemicals
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses which mutations are inherited (sex cells vs body cells) but does not describe mutations as changes in DNA or chromosomes, nor does it discuss factors that cause mutations such as infectious agents, radiation, or chemicals. It only touches on the inheritance aspect, which is not a substantive part of the competency.

copy.en:
Which mutations get passed to kids?

If a mutation happens in reproductive cells, it can be passed down to the offspring. But if it happens in other body cells, it isn't inherited at all.
copy.tl:
Aling mutation ang naipapasa sa anak?

Kung nangyari ang mutation sa mga selulang pang-reproduksyon, maipapasa ito sa mga anak. Pero kung sa ibang selula ito nangyari, hindi ito namamana.
copy.bis:
Unsang mutation ang mapasa sa anak?

Kung mahitabo ang mutation sa mga selula sa pagpadaghan, mahimo kining ipasa sa mga anak. Apan kung sa ubang selula kini mahitabo, dili gyud kini mapanunod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That is called mutualism, a type of interaction where both species benefit from the relationship!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches mutualism as a species interaction; it does not identify landforms or bodies of water or describe their influence on living and non-living components.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That is called mutualism, a type of interaction where both species benefit from the relationship!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a beneficial interaction between living things, not about protecting or conserving the environment for survival.

copy.en:
What if two living things both get something good from helping each other?

That is called mutualism, a type of interaction where both species benefit from the relationship!
copy.tl:
Paano kung parehong may nakukuhang mabuti ang dalawang may buhay sa pagtulong sa isa't isa?

Iyan ang tinatawag na mutualism, isang uri ng interaksyon kung saan parehong nakikinabang ang dalawang species sa relasyon!
copy.bis:
Unsa man kung ang duha ka buhi nga butang parehong makakuha og maayo sa pagtinabangay?

Kana gitawag og mutualism, usa ka klase sa interaksyon diin ang duha ka species parehong makabenepisyo sa relasyon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The skin under your nail actually has nerves, so it hurts if the nail is cut too short.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains pain from cutting nails due to nerves in the skin, which relates to the nervous system, not any of the five systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) listed in G4-L-1. It shares the broad subject of human body but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Why does it hurt to cut your nail too short?

The skin under your nail actually has nerves, so it hurts if the nail is cut too short.
copy.tl:
Bakit masakit kapag sobra ang putol sa kuko?

Ang balat sa ilalim ng kuko ay may ugat ng pakiramdam, kaya masakit kapag naputol ito nang sobra.
copy.bis:
Nganong sakit kung sobra ka mubo ang putol sa kuko?

Ang panit ilalom sa kuko adunay nerbiyo, mao nga masakit kung sobra ka mubo ang pagputol niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The farad unit is named after Michael Faraday, a British scientist who studied electricity and magnetism!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies Michael Faraday as a famous foreign scientist, but it does not identify any invention of his. The competency requires identifying a scientist and their invention/s, so the card only shares the scientist's name and field of study, not the invention itself.

copy.en: The farad unit is named after Michael Faraday, a British scientist who studied electricity and magnetism!
copy.tl: Ang yunit na farad ay ipinangalan kay Michael Faraday, isang Britanong siyentista na nag-aral ng kuryente at magnetismo!
copy.bis: Ang yunit nga farad ginganlan kang Michael Faraday, usa ka Britaniko nga siyentista nga nagtuon sa koryente ug magnetismo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hardwood comes from strong trees that grow slowly, like the narra.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the origin/meaning of the term 'hardwood' (from slow-growing strong trees) but does not describe the physical property of hardness or any other solid-material property (hard, shiny, stretchable). It shares vocabulary ('hard') but provides no direct instructional support for describing physical properties.

copy.en:
What makes wood a 'hardwood'?

Hardwood comes from strong trees that grow slowly, like the narra.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng hardwood?

Ang hardwood o matigas na kahoy ay galing sa mga punong matibay at mabagal lumaki, tulad ng narra.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang buot ipasabot sa hardwood?

Ang hardwood o gahi nga kahoy gikan sa lig-on ug hinay motubo nga kahoy, sama sa narra.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The narra tree blooms with small, yellow, fragrant flowers.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a flower of the narra tree, but the competency requires observing outer plant parts such as leaves, roots, and stems and identifying their role in obtaining water and nutrients. Flowers are not among the listed parts and no function related to water/nutrient uptake is addressed.

copy.en: The narra tree blooms with small, yellow, fragrant flowers.
copy.tl: Namumulaklak ang narra ng maliliit, dilaw, at mababangong bulaklak.
copy.bis: Ang narra mamulak og gagmay, dalag, ug humot nga mga bulak.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Once nata gets thick enough, it's lifted out like one big clear mat, washed, cooked, then cut into the little cubes you see in your dessert glass!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify the products of traditional biotechnology through fermentation (e.g. cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, nata de coco)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the post-fermentation processing of nata de coco (washing, cooking, cutting into cubes) but does not identify nata de coco as a product of traditional biotechnology through fermentation, nor mention fermentation or the role of microorganisms. It shares the topic (nata de coco) but does not directly support the competency's skill of identifying fermentation-based biotech products.

copy.en: Once nata gets thick enough, it's lifted out like one big clear mat, washed, cooked, then cut into the little cubes you see in your dessert glass!
copy.tl: Kapag sapat na kapal ang nata, inaalis ito na parang isang malaking malinaw na kutson, hinuhugasan, niluluto, at hinihiwa sa maliliit na kwadrado na nakikita mo sa iyong panghimagas!
copy.bis: Kung baga na ang nata, kuhaon kini nga daw usa ka dako ug tin-aw nga banig, hugasan, lutoon, ug putlon sa gagmay nga kwadrado nga makita nimo sa imong panghimagas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pigs barely sweat, so mud helps cool them down when it's hot.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavioral adaptation (mud rolling) that helps pigs cope with heat and insects, but it does not describe how animals have 'changed' over time to suit their environment, nor does it use secondary sources. It is a single example of an animal behavior, not an explanation of evolutionary change or adaptation as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pigs barely sweat, so mud helps cool them down when it's hot.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a pig's cooling behavior, which is a response to the environment, but it does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). The response to heat is an example of responding, but the card does not frame it as a characteristic of living things or address growth or reproduction. It is only tangentially related to the competency.

copy.en:
Why do pigs roll in mud?

Pigs barely sweat, so mud helps cool them down when it's hot. It also shields their skin from the sun and biting insects!
copy.tl:
Bakit naglulublob ang baboy sa putik?

Hindi gaanong pumapawis ang baboy kaya nakakatulong ang putik para magpalamig sa init. Nakakaprotekta rin ito sa balat nila mula sa araw at mga kagat ng insekto!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga maglunang ang baboy sa lapok?

Dili kaayo mosingot ang baboy mao nga makatabang ang lapok para pabugnawon sila sa init. Nagpanalipod usab kini sa ilang panit gikan sa adlaw ug mga paak sa insekto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Both have tusks, but the warthog has a bigger head with warty bumps on its face
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card compares two specific animals but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (mammals, reptiles, etc.). It only mentions that different wild pigs live in different parts of the world, which is not classification into the required groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: different wild pigs live in different parts of the world
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a drawing or diagram to classify Philippine animals/plants by habitat (terrestrial, aquatic, aerial). It only notes geographic distribution of wild pigs, not habitat classification, and no drawing/diagram is present.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Both have tusks, but the warthog has a bigger head with warty bumps on its face
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions outer body parts (tusks, head, warty bumps) but does not identify their role in movement or gathering food. It does not describe how these parts help the animal move or obtain food, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How is the Philippine wild pig different from an African warthog?

Both have tusks, but the warthog has a bigger head with warty bumps on its face — different wild pigs live in different parts of the world.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng baboy-ramo natin sa warthog ng Africa?

Magkapareho silang may pangil, pero mas malaki ang ulo at may bukol sa mukha ang warthog — iba't ibang lahi ng baboy ang nakatira sa iba't ibang bahagi ng mundo.
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa baboy-ihalas nato ug sa warthog sa Africa?

Pareho silang adunay bangkil, apan mas dako ang ulo ug adunay bukol sa nawong ang warthog — lain-laing lahi sa baboy ihalas ang nagpuyo sa lain-laing bahin sa kalibotan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cotton comes from the cotton plant! After flowering, it forms a fluffy boll that bursts open to show soft white fibers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes cotton fiber from the cotton plant's seed pod (boll) and its use in clothing. It does not address the outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in obtaining water and nutrients from the soil, which is the focus of G3-L-5. The content is only broadly related to plants.

copy.en: Cotton comes from the cotton plant! After flowering, it forms a fluffy boll that bursts open to show soft white fibers, which are spun into thread for clothes.
copy.tl: Ang cotton ay galing sa cotton plant! Pagkatapos mamulaklag, bubuo ito ng fluffy boll na bubuka para ipakita ang malalambot na puting fibers na ginagawang sinulid para sa damit.
copy.bis: Ang cotton naggikan sa cotton plant! Human mamulak, mahimo kini nga fluffy boll nga mobuka ug mogawas ang humok nga puti nga fibers nga himuong tanod para sa sinina.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It comes from latex, a white milky sap from rubber trees
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions rubber trees and latex sap, but does not describe outer plant parts such as leaves, roots, or stems or their roles in taking up water and nutrients. It only relates to plants in a general way.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It comes from latex, a white milky sap from rubber trees
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies natural rubber as coming from latex of a living rubber tree. The competency concerns useful things made from non-living materials and the natural non-living materials used. Rubber from a plant is a living-source material, so the card does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en:
Where does natural rubber actually come from?

It comes from latex, a white milky sap from rubber trees (Hevea brasiliensis), which the Philippines grows mostly in Mindanao!
copy.tl:
Saan ba talaga nagmumula ang natural na goma?

Galing ito sa latex, isang puting malagkit na sap mula sa rubber tree (Hevea brasiliensis) na maraming tumutubo sa Mindanao!
copy.bis:
Asa man gani naggikan ang natural nga goma?

Gikan kini sa latex, usa ka puting gataon nga sap gikan sa rubber tree (Hevea brasiliensis) nga daghan motubo sa Mindanao!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It fills these chambers with gas or water to float up or sink down.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes buoyancy control using shell chambers, which relates to movement but does not describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their role in moving and gathering food as required by G3-L-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It fills these chambers with gas or water to float up or sink down.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavioral/structural mechanism for buoyancy, but does not describe how the nautilus has changed to better suit its environment through mimicry, camouflage, or similar adaptations. It does not directly support the competency's focus on evolutionary adaptation.

copy.en: The nautilus is a sea animal with a thick spiral shell divided into chambers. It fills these chambers with gas or water to float up or sink down.
copy.tl: Ang nautilus ay hayop sa dagat na may makapal na paikot-ikot na kabibe na hati-hati sa mga silid. Pinupuno nito ng hangin o tubig ang mga silid para lumutang o lumubog.
copy.bis: Ang nautilus usa ka hayop sa dagat nga adunay baga nga nagliko-liko nga kabibe nga gibahin sa mga lawak. Gipuno niini og hangin o tubig ang mga lawak aron molutaw o molunod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Animals usually rely on more than one cue to navigate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about animals using multiple navigation cues (sun, stars, magnetic field, smell). It does not describe animals changing to better suit their environment, nor mimicry or camouflage, so it does not support G5-L-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Animals usually rely on more than one cue to navigate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes animal behavior but does not teach the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). Responding to cues is only loosely related to the competency's 'respond' characteristic, with no direct instructional support.

copy.en: Animals usually rely on more than one cue to navigate — when clouds hide the sun or stars, they switch to Earth's magnetic field or smell as a backup so they don't get lost.
copy.tl: Karaniwang gumagamit ang mga hayop ng higit sa isang palatandaan — kapag natatakpan ng ulap ang araw o bituin, lumilipat sila sa magnetic field o amoy bilang backup para hindi mawala.
copy.bis: Kasagaran ang mananap mogamit og labaw sa usa ka timailhan — kung tabunan sa panganod ang adlaw o bituon, mobalhin sila sa magnetic field o baho isip backup aron dili mawala.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A nearsighted person sees things up close clearly, but faraway things look blurry
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines nearsightedness (myopia), which is an everyday example related to how the eye refracts light, but it does not describe or illustrate reflection or refraction using mirrors, lenses, prisms, or any investigation. It provides no instructional support for the competency's required activities or concepts.

copy.en:
What is nearsightedness?

A nearsighted person sees things up close clearly, but faraway things look blurry — that's called myopia.
copy.tl:
Ano ang myopia?

Malinaw makita ng taong may myopia ang malapit na bagay, pero malabo sa kanya ang malayo — tinatawag itong myopia.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang myopia?

Klaro makita sa tawong adunay myopia ang duol nga butang, apan hanap sa iya ang layo — gitawag kini og myopia.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each kidney holds about a million tiny filters called nephrons — they do the real work of cleaning your blood!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about nephrons filtering blood, which is part of the excretory system. However, G8-L-2 requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). The card uses no such representation and does not explain any system interaction; it only provides a single isolated fact about kidney function.

copy.en: Each kidney holds about a million tiny filters called nephrons — they do the real work of cleaning your blood!
copy.tl: Bawat bato ay may halos isang milyong maliliit na salaan na tinatawag na nephrons — sila ang tunay na naglilinis ng iyong dugo!
copy.bis: Matag kidney adunay halos usa ka milyon ka gagmayng salaan nga gitawag og nephrons — sila ang tinuod nga naghinlo sa imong dugo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Neptune is the last major planet to be discovered!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a historical fact about Neptune's discovery year. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, identify major celestial objects' features, or discuss composition, which are the core actions of G5-E-11.

copy.en:
Which planet was the last major one to be discovered?

Neptune is the last major planet to be discovered! Scientists finally found it in the year 1846.
copy.tl:
Anong planeta ang huling pangunahing planetang natuklasan?

Ang Neptune ang huling pangunahing planetang natuklasan! Natuklasan lang ito ng mga siyentipiko noong 1846.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga planeta ang ulahing dakong planeta nga nadiskobre?

Ang Neptune mao ang ulahing dakong planeta nga nadiskobre! Nadiskobre lang kini sa mga siyentipiko niadtong 1846.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Neptune has the strongest winds of any planet!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single fact about Neptune's winds, but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, identify major celestial objects' names, main features, or composition. It is only tangentially related to the solar system topic.

copy.en: Neptune has the strongest winds of any planet! They can reach 2,100 kilometres per hour — faster than the strongest typhoon on Earth!
copy.tl: Ang Neptune ang may pinakamalakas na hangin sa lahat ng planeta! Umaabot ng 2,100 kilometro bawat oras — mas mabilis pa kaysa pinakamalakas na typhoon sa Earth!
copy.bis: Ang Neptune adunay pinakakusog nga hangin sa tanang planeta! Makaabot og 2,100 kilometro matag oras — mas paspas pa kaysa pinakakusog nga typhoon sa Yuta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A nerve cell, or neuron, carries signals like tiny electrical messages

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the function of a single nerve cell (neuron) in carrying signals. Animals need specific spots to build nests — without trees and forests, they can't reproduce well and their numbers may drop.

Bakit mahalaga ang kagubatan para sa pugad ng hayop?

Kailangan ng mga hayop ng tiyak na lugar para sa kanilang pugad — kung mawala ang puno at kagubatan, hindi na sila makakapagparami nang maayos.
copy.bis:
Nganong importante ang kalasangan para sa salag sa mananap?

Ang mga mananap nanginahanglan og piho nga lugar para sa ilang salag — kon mawala ang kahoy ug kalasangan, dili na sila makapadaghan og maayo.

What is a neuron?

It's a special cell that sends fast electrical signals so your brain can talk to the rest of your body.

Isa itong espesyal na selula na nagpapadala ng mabilisang elektrikal na senyales para makipag-usap ang utak sa buong katawan.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang neuron?

Usa kini ka pinasahi nga selula nga nagpadala og paspas nga elektrikal nga senyales aron makigsulti ang utok sa tibuok lawas.

copy.tl: Ang neuron ay nerve cell na nagpapadala ng mensahe bilang maliliit na electrical signal. Bilyon-bilyon ang magkakaugnay na bumubuo sa utak at nerves, at sobrang bilis nilang ipasa ang signal sa buong katawan.
copy.bis: Ang neuron usa ka nerve cell nga magpadala og mensahe isip gagmayng electrical signal. Bilyon-bilyon ang nagkadugtong nga naghimo sa utok ug nerves, ug paspas kaayo silang mopadala og signal sa tibuok lawas.

Why put baking soda or vinegar on an ant or bee sting?

Some stings are acidic, so a mild base like baking soda can neutralize them for relief. But always ask a doctor first, since not all stings are the same!
copy.tl:
Bakit nilalagyan ng baking soda o suka ang kagat ng langgam o bubuyog?

Ang ilang kagat ay acidic, kaya ang baking soda ay pwedeng mag-neutralize at makapagpaginhawa. Pero magtanong muna sa doktor, dahil hindi lahat ng kagat ay pareho!
copy.bis:
Ngano butangan og baking soda o suka ang paak sa langgam o buyog?

Ang uban nga paak kay acidic, busa ang baking soda makahimo og neutralize ug makahatag og kahupayan. Apan mangutana una sa doktor, kay dili tanan nga paak parehas!

copy.en: Neutralization and dilution are different! Diluting just adds water to weaken the acid, but it's still acid. Neutralizing adds a base to truly change it into salt and water.
copy.tl: Iba ang neutralization sa dilution! Sa dilution, dinadagdagan mo lang ng tubig para humina ang asido. Sa neutralization, nagdadagdag ka ng base para talagang maging asin at tubig ito.
copy.bis: Lahi ang neutralization sa dilution! Sa dilution, magdugang lang ka og tubig aron mohuyang ang asido. Sa neutralization, magdugang ka og base aron tinuod nga mahimo kining asin ug tubig.

The New Horizons probe explored the dwarf planet Pluto! It took amazing pictures of this distant world.

He published them in the year 1687 in his book called the Principia!

Inilathala niya sila noong taong 1687 sa kanyang aklat na tinatawag na Principia!
copy.bis:
Kanus-a ug asa gipatik ni Isaac Newton ang iyang mga balaod sa paglihok?

Gipatik niya kini niadtong tuig 1687 sa iyang libro nga gitawag og Principia!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s

A smart scientist named Isaac Newton formulated the three laws of motion to explain how things move!

Sino ang bumuo ng tatlong batas ng galaw?

Isang matalinong siyentipiko na si Isaac Newton ang bumuo ng tatlong batas ng galaw (three laws of motion) para ipaliwanag kung paano gumagalaw ang mga bagay!
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang naghimo sa tulo ka balaod sa paglihok?

Usa ka maalamon nga siyentipiko nga si Isaac Newton ang naghimo sa tulo ka balaod sa paglihok (three laws of motion) aron masabtan kung giunsa paglihok sa mga butang!

copy.bis: Ang mga dahon sa nipa palm mao ang atop sa tradisyonal nga bahay kubo! Kon sinomlong nang maayo, natural kini nga water-resistant ug nagpabugnaw sa sulod.

copy.tl: Bukod sa pang-atip, ginagamit din ang mga dahon ng nipa bilang dingding at pambalot ng katutubong sigarilyo.

A climbing vine with fragrant flowers that change color from white to red as they get older.
copy.tl:
Ano ang kakaiba sa bulaklak ng niyog-niyogan?

Gumagapang na baging na may mababangong bulaklak na nagbabago ng kulay mula puti hanggang pula habang tumatanda.
copy.bis:
Unsay talagsaon sa bulak sa niyog-niyogan?

Usa ka nagakamang nga baging nga adunay humot nga bulak nga nag-usab og kolor gikan puti ngadto pula samtang motigulang.

assignedReviews.reason: General asexual/no-gamete biology never names plants, pollination, seed production, or plant propagation.

Does asexual reproduction need a sperm and an egg?

No! There is no fertilization and no gamete formation in this mode of reproduction.
copy.tl:
Kailangan ba ng asexual reproduction ng isang sperm at isang egg?

Hindi! Walang fertilization at walang gamete formation sa ganitong paraan ng reproduction.

Kinahanglan ba sa asexual reproduction ang usa ka sperm ug usa ka egg?

Dili! Walay fertilization ug walay gamete formation sa ingon ani nga paagi sa reproduction.

What makes noble gases so special?

Noble gases like helium, neon, and argon rarely react with other elements!

Ano ang nagpapaka-espesyal sa mga noble gas?

Kabilang sa mga noble gas ang helium, neon, at argon — bihirang makipagreaksyon sa iba!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang naghimo sa noble gases nga espesyal?

Ang noble gases naglakip sa helium, neon, ug argon — panagsa ra mo-react sa uban!

Why can nocturnal animals see so well at night?

Nocturnal animals' eyes have more rod cells that work well in dim light, so they see well in the dark but not so well in color.

Bakit maganda ang paningin sa dilim ng nokturnal na hayop?

Ang mata ng nokturnal na hayop ay may mas maraming rod cell na mabuti sa mahinang liwanag, kaya mahusay silang makakita sa dilim pero mahina sa kulay.
copy.bis:
Ngano maayo makakita sa kangitngit ang nokturnal nga mananap?

Ang mata sa nokturnal nga mananap adunay mas daghang rod cell nga maayo sa huyang nga kahayag, mao nga maayo silang makakita sa kangitngit apan luya sa kolor.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions loudness of a normal conversation, which is related to sound, but it does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred. It only states a typical decibel level, so it does not directly support the competency.

How loud is a normal chat with your friends?

A normal conversation is about 60 decibels (dB) loud!
copy.tl:
Gaano kalakas ang isang karaniwang usapan?

Ang lakas ng karaniwang usapan ay nasa mga 60 desibel (dB)!
copy.bis:
Unsa kab kusog ang ordinaryong panagsultihay?

Ang ordinaryong panagsultihay anaa sa mga 60 desibel (dB) ka kusog!

How do we get nuclear energy?

It comes from splitting uranium atoms! This releases huge heat that is turned into electricity.
copy.tl:
Paano natin makuha ang nuclear energy?

Galing ito sa paghahati ng atomo ng uranium! Naglalabas ito ng napakalaking init na ginagawang kuryente.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkuha sa nuclear energy?

Gikan kini sa pagbahin sa atomo sa uranium! Nagpagawas kini ug dakong init nga himuon nga koryente.

copy.en:
Can you feel glucagon working?

You can never feel glucagon working — it quietly adjusts your blood sugar every single day without you noticing.
copy.tl:
Nararamdaman mo ba ang glucagon?

Hindi mo talaga nararamdaman ang glucagon — tahimik nitong inaayos ang asukal sa iyong dugo araw-araw.
copy.bis:
Mabati ba nimo ang glucagon?

Dili gyud nimo mabati ang glucagon — hilom kining nag-ayo sa asukal sa imong dugo matag adlaw.

copy.en:
How does insulin let sugar into cells?

Sugar needs a 'key' to enter cells and become energy — insulin is that key. When insulin touches a cell, it's like a door opens and sugar goes in.
copy.tl:
Paano pinapapasok ng insulin ang asukal sa selula?

Kailangan ng asukal ng 'susi' para makapasok sa selula at gawing enerhiya — ang insulin ang susing iyon. Kapag dumikit ito sa selula, parang nabubuksan ang pinto at nakakapasok ang asukal.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagpasulod sa insulin sa asukal sa selula?

Ang asukal nagkinahanglan og 'yawe' aron makasulod sa selula ug mahimong enerhiya — ang insulin mao kana nga yawe. Kung modikit kini sa selula, mura'g maabli ang pultahan ug makasulod ang asukal.

copy.en:
Why does high blood sugar make you tired?

Without enough insulin, sugar can't enter the cells for energy — even though the blood is full of it. That's why you feel tired or weak.
copy.tl:
Bakit nakakapagod ang mataas na blood sugar?

Kapag kulang sa insulin, hindi makapasok ang asukal sa mga selula para sa enerhiya — kahit puno ng asukal ang dugo. Kaya napapagod o nanghihina ka.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga makapakapoy ang taas nga blood sugar?

Kon kulang ang insulin, dili makasulod ang asukal sa mga selula para sa enerhiya — bisan puno na sa asukal ang dugo. Mao nga gikapoy o gluya ka.

Does curling into a ball always protect the pangolin?

Not from humans! Rolling into a ball saves it from lions, but it actually makes it easier for people to just pick up.
copy.tl:
Laging ba nakakaprotekta ang pagbilog ng pangolin?

Hindi laban sa tao! Nagliligtas ang pagbilog nito laban sa leon, pero mas madali pa itong mahuli ng tao dahil dito.

Kanunay ba nga naprotektahan ang pangolin kung mokoyokoy?

Dili batok sa tawo! Ang pagligid nga morag bola makaluwas niini batok sa leon, apan mas sayon hinuon kining hakopon sa tawo.
